lessons.title: Selecting Hinges, Latches, and Handles
lessons.body:
When choosing hinges for a gate, the first thing to check is the weight of the gate leaf. A typical wooden gate 1.2 m wide and 1.8 m high weighs about 40â50 kg. For that, use three 100 mm (4 inch) galvanised steel T-hinges or strap hinges. For metal gates up to 80 kg, use 150 mm (6 inch) heavy-duty weld-on hinges. In Africa, where rust is a constant enemy, always choose hot-dip galvanised or stainless steel hardware. Avoid cheap painted hinges; they fail within a year in coastal or humid areas.

Latches must be easy to operate but secure. A simple sliding bolt latch (200 mm long) works for most residential gates. For double gates, use a drop rod or a double-sided latch so you can open from either side. Handles should be comfortable and rust-resistant. A 200 mm pull handle with a powder-coated finish is good. In dusty regions, avoid intricate locking mechanisms that jam. A heavy-duty padlock hasp (100 mm) is often more reliable than a built-in lock.

For metal gates, weld hinges directly to the frame and post. For wooden gates, use carriage bolts (M10 x 100 mm) with washers and nuts. Always drill pilot holes to prevent splitting. In sandy or rocky soil, ensure the gate post is set in concrete at least 600 mm deep. The hinge must be aligned so the gate swings freely without dragging. A common mistake is using hinges that are too small; they bend under weight. Always go one size up from what you think you need.

In rural areas, you can find blacksmith-made hinges that are strong and cheap. Test them for smooth movement. For latches, a simple gravity latch with a spring works well. Remember, hardware is the weakest link. Buy the best you can afford; replacing a broken hinge is harder than installing a good one from the start.

lessons.title: Installing Gate Hardware for Wood and Metal Gates
lessons.body:
Installing hardware starts with marking. For a wooden gate, hold the hinge in place, mark screw holes with a pencil, then drill pilot holes 2 mm smaller than the screw diameter. Use 8 mm x 75 mm coach screws for heavy gates. For metal gates, clamp the hinge and weld it with a 2.5 mm welding rod at 90â110 amps. If you cannot weld, use M10 bolts with lock nuts. Always install the bottom hinge first, then the top hinge. Check that the gate is level and has a 10â15 mm gap from the ground.

For latches, position the catch so the bolt slides smoothly into the keeper. On wooden gates, chisel a shallow recess for the latch plate so it sits flush. On metal gates, weld or bolt the latch. The handle should be at a comfortable height, about 1 metre from the ground. For double gates, install a drop rod in the centre. Test the gate swing: it should open and close with one hand. If it binds, adjust the hinges by adding washers or bending the hinge pin slightly.

Safety is key. After installation, check that no bolts protrude to cut hands. File sharp edges. In Africa, where gates are often used by children, ensure latches are child-safe but not easily opened by toddlers. A spring-loaded latch is better than a simple sliding bolt. For metal gates, paint all welds with zinc-rich primer to prevent rust. For wooden gates, apply wood preservative to the hinge area.

Common problems: sagging gate (tighten top hinge or add a diagonal brace), sticking latch (file the keeper or adjust alignment), loose hinge (replace screws with longer ones or use through-bolts). Always use a spirit level and a square. A gate that is not square will never hang right. Take your time; a good installation lasts 10 years or more.

lessons.title: Introduction to Automatic Gate Openers
lessons.body:
Automatic gate openers save time and add security. There are three main types: swing arm (for single gates up to 2.5 m wide), sliding (for gates up to 6 m wide), and underground (for heavy gates). For a typical African home, a 24V DC swing arm opener is common because it works with a battery backup during power cuts. Prices range from $200 to $800. Choose a kit with a control board, two remotes, and a safety sensor.

Before buying, check the gate weight and width. A 1.8 m high, 3 m wide steel gate can weigh 150 kg. You need an opener rated for at least 200 kg. The opener arm must be mounted on a solid pillar; a weak post will cause misalignment. For sliding gates, install a rack and pinion system. The motor moves the gate along a track. Ensure the track is free of debris and the gate wheels are in good condition.

Power supply is critical. In areas with frequent outages, use a 12V or 24V battery with a solar panel (100W) and charge controller. A 7Ah battery lasts about 2 days without sun. For swing openers, the arm must be installed at a 90-degree angle when the gate is closed. Follow the manufacturer's template. Set the limit switches so the gate stops exactly at open and closed positions. Test manually before connecting power.

Safety is non-negotiable. Automatic gates can crush. Install safety sensors (photocells) across the opening. If the beam is broken, the gate reverses. Also, set the force limit so the gate stops if it hits an obstacle. In Africa, where power surges are common, use a surge protector. A qualified electrician should do the wiring. Never run 220V cables in the same conduit as low-voltage sensor wires. Keep the control box locked and dry. Regular maintenance is needed: lubricate the arm every 3 months, check battery water levels (if lead-acid), and clean the track.

lessons.title: Wiring and Safety Sensors for Automatic Gates
lessons.body:
Wiring an automatic gate requires care. First, turn off the main power. Use a 3-core cable (1.5 mmÂ²) for 220V supply to the control box. For low-voltage sensors and keypads, use 2-core shielded cable (0.5 mmÂ²) to avoid interference. Run cables in PVC conduit buried 300 mm deep or fixed to the wall. Never mix high and low voltage in the same conduit. Connect the motor wires to the control board terminals marked MOTOR 1 and MOTOR 2. For a swing opener, connect the positive and negative according to the manual. If the gate opens when it should close, swap the wires.

Safety sensors are photocells. Mount one on each side of the gate opening, about 150 mm above ground. Align them so the red LED on the receiver is steady. When the beam is broken, the gate should stop and reverse. Test by walking through. Also install a flashing light and a warning sign. For sliding gates, add a safety edge (rubber strip) on the leading edge. It stops the gate if it touches an obstacle.

Connect the sensor wires to the control board terminals marked PHOTO or SAFETY. Most boards have a common and a signal terminal. Use a multimeter to check continuity. If the sensor does not work, check for dust on the lenses, misalignment, or broken wires. In dusty areas, clean the lenses weekly. For battery backup, connect a 12V 7Ah battery to the board's BAT terminals. Use a solar panel with a charge controller if mains power is unreliable.

Always earth the gate and control box. Use a 1.5 m copper earth rod driven into the ground and connect with 6 mmÂ² green/yellow wire. This prevents electric shock. After wiring, test all functions: open, close, stop, reverse, and remote. If the gate reverses immediately after closing, the limit switch is set too tight. Adjust it. Keep wiring diagrams in a plastic sleeve near the control box. Label all cables. A neat installation is easier to troubleshoot.

lessons.title: Programming and Remote Control Setup
lessons.body:
Programming a gate opener starts with the control board. Most boards have a learn button. To add a remote, press the learn button once (LED blinks), then press the remote button within 5 seconds. The LED stops blinking. Test the remote. To delete all remotes, hold the learn button for 10 seconds. For rolling code remotes, you may need to press the remote twice. If the remote range is short, extend the antenna wire or replace the battery (usually 12V A23).

Set the open and close limits. Use the manual release to move the gate to the desired open position. Then turn the limit adjustment screw until the microswitch clicks. Do the same for closed. Run the gate to test. If it overshoots, adjust the screw. For sliding gates, set the deceleration so the gate slows before hitting the limit. This reduces wear. Also set the auto-close timer: typically 30â60 seconds. For safety, enable the reverse on obstacle function.

For multiple users, you can program a keypad or a GSM module. A keypad allows entry with a code. A GSM module lets you open the gate with a phone call. These connect to the control board's accessory terminals. In Africa, where cellphone coverage is good, GSM openers are popular. They cost about $50. Follow the module's manual to insert a SIM card and set authorized numbers.

Troubleshooting: remote not working â check battery, re-learn, or check antenna. Gate opens but does not close â safety sensor is blocked or faulty. Gate moves in wrong direction â swap motor wires. Beeping sound â battery low. Always keep a spare remote and battery. Write down the programming steps in a notebook. If you change the control board, you will need to reprogram everything. Test the system weekly: open and close the gate, check the sensors, and listen for unusual noises.

lessons.title: Maintenance of Gate Hardware and Openers
lessons.body:
A maintenance schedule prevents breakdowns. Every month, check hinges, latches, and handles. Tighten any loose screws. Apply a few drops of oil (SAE 30) to hinge pins. For metal gates, touch up any rust spots with a wire brush and zinc primer, then paint. In coastal areas, do this every 2 months. For wooden gates, check for rot around hinges; replace soft wood with a hardwood patch. Sand and repaint.

Every 3 months, service the automatic opener. Open the control box and check for moisture, insects, or corrosion. Clean the board with a soft brush. Check battery terminals; clean with baking soda and water if corroded. For lead-acid batteries, top up with distilled water if low. Test the battery voltage: a 12V battery should read 12.6V when fully charged. If below 11.8V, recharge or replace. For solar panels, clean the glass with a damp cloth.

Lubricate the opener arm or track with lithium grease. For swing arms, grease the pivot points. For sliding gates, clean the track and apply a dry lubricant (graphite) to avoid attracting dust. Check the gate wheels; replace if worn. Test the safety sensors by blocking the beam; the gate should reverse. If not, clean lenses and realign. Test the manual release: it should work smoothly in case of power failure.

Every 6 months, check the gate alignment. If the gate sags, adjust the hinges or add a brace. Check the post for looseness; tighten bolts or re-concrete. Inspect all wiring for cracks or rodent damage. Replace any damaged cable. Keep a logbook: date, work done, parts replaced. In Africa, where dust and heat are harsh, shorten intervals to every 2 months for hardware and every 2 months for openers. A well-maintained gate lasts 15 years. A neglected one fails in 2. Spend 30 minutes a month; it saves hundreds in repairs.

quiz.q: What is the minimum recommended depth for setting a gate post in concrete?
quiz.explanation: A depth of at least 600 mm ensures the post is stable and prevents sagging.

quiz.q: Which type of hinge is best for a heavy metal gate up to 80 kg?
quiz.explanation: 150 mm weld-on hinges are designed for heavy metal gates and provide strong support.

quiz.q: Why should you avoid painted hinges in coastal areas?
options: C) They are hard to install
D) They are not strong enough
quiz.explanation: Painted hinges corrode fast in humid, salty air, leading to early failure.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a drop rod on a double gate?
options: A) To lock the gate from the top
B) To secure the centre of the gate
C) To hold the gate open
quiz.explanation: A drop rod secures the centre of double gates, preventing them from being forced open.

quiz.q: When installing hardware on a wooden gate, what should you do before driving screws?
options: A) Soak the wood in water
quiz.explanation: Pilot holes prevent the wood from splitting and ensure screws go in straight.

quiz.q: What is the recommended gap between the bottom of a gate and the ground?
quiz.explanation: A 10â15 mm gap allows the gate to swing freely without dragging.

quiz.q: Which tool is essential for checking that a gate is level?
quiz.explanation: A spirit level ensures the gate is horizontally and vertically aligned.

quiz.q: What should you do if a gate sags after installation?
options: B) Tighten the top hinge or add a brace
quiz.explanation: Sagging is often fixed by adjusting the top hinge or adding a diagonal brace.

quiz.q: Which type of automatic gate opener is best for a sliding gate up to 6 m wide?
quiz.explanation: Sliding openers are designed for wide sliding gates and use a rack and pinion system.

quiz.q: What voltage is commonly used for residential automatic gate openers in Africa?
quiz.explanation: 24V DC openers are popular because they can run on battery backup during power cuts.

quiz.q: Why is a solar panel useful for an automatic gate?
options: A) It makes the gate faster
B) It charges the battery during power outages
quiz.explanation: A solar panel keeps the battery charged when mains power is unavailable.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of limit switches in an automatic gate?
options: B) To stop the gate at open and closed positions
D) To limit the remote range
quiz.explanation: Limit switches tell the motor when to stop at the fully open or closed position.

quiz.q: What should you do before connecting power to a new automatic gate opener?
quiz.explanation: Manual testing ensures the gate moves freely and the mechanism is not jammed.

quiz.q: Which cable size is recommended for 220V supply to a gate control box?
quiz.explanation: 1.5 mmÂ² 3-core cable is adequate for the current draw of most gate openers.

quiz.q: Why should low-voltage sensor wires not share conduit with 220V cables?
quiz.explanation: High voltage can induce noise in low-voltage wires, causing false sensor readings.

quiz.q: What is the function of a photocell in an automatic gate system?
options: A) To detect light for the motor
B) To detect obstacles and reverse the gate
D) To open the gate remotely
quiz.explanation: Photocells create an invisible beam; if broken, the gate stops or reverses to prevent injury.

quiz.q: How high above the ground should safety photocells be mounted?
quiz.explanation: 150 mm is a standard height to detect small obstacles like pets or children.

quiz.q: What should you do if the gate reverses immediately after closing?
quiz.explanation: The limit switch is set too tight, causing the gate to think it hit an obstacle.

quiz.q: Why is earthing important for an automatic gate?
options: C) To make the gate faster
quiz.explanation: Earthing protects users from electric shock if a fault occurs.

quiz.q: How do you add a new remote to most gate control boards?
options: A) Press the learn button then the remote button
B) Turn off power and on again
C) Use a screwdriver to adjust
quiz.explanation: The learn button puts the board in pairing mode; pressing the remote button stores the code.

quiz.q: What is the typical auto-close timer setting for a residential gate?
quiz.explanation: 30â60 seconds gives enough time for a vehicle to pass without leaving the gate open too long.

quiz.q: What does a GSM module allow you to do with an automatic gate?
options: A) Open it with a phone call
B) Open it with a remote
D) Open it with a key
quiz.explanation: A GSM module connects to the cell network, so you can call the gate to open it.

quiz.q: Why should you keep a logbook for gate maintenance?
options: A) To track work done and parts replaced
quiz.explanation: A logbook helps you remember when maintenance was last done and what was replaced.

quiz.q: How often should you lubricate the hinge pins on a gate?
quiz.explanation: Monthly oiling keeps hinges moving freely and prevents squeaks and wear.

quiz.q: What should you use to clean corroded battery terminals?
quiz.explanation: Baking soda neutralises acid corrosion and cleans the terminals safely.

quiz.q: What voltage should a fully charged 12V lead-acid battery read?
quiz.explanation: 12.6V indicates a fully charged battery; below 11.8V it needs recharging.

quiz.q: What lubricant is best for a sliding gate track in dusty conditions?
quiz.explanation: Dry graphite does not attract dust, unlike oil or grease.

quiz.q: How often should you test the manual release on an automatic gate?
quiz.explanation: Regular testing ensures the release works when you need it during a power cut.

quiz.q: What is a sign that a gate post may be loose?
options: B) The gate sags or wobbles
quiz.explanation: A loose post causes the gate to sag or wobble, affecting alignment.

quiz.q: In dusty African conditions, how often should you clean photocell lenses?
quiz.explanation: Dust can block the beam, so weekly cleaning ensures reliable safety operation.
